findings.title: Duplicate downsize definition overwrites 4-arg version
findings.body: File app/models/optimized_image.rb defines self.downsize twice: line 145 as (from,to,max_width,max_height,opts) and line 149 as (from,to,dimensions,opts). Ruby has no overloading, so the second definition replaces the first and the first becomes dead code. Any existing caller using the 4-argument form will bind max_width to dimensions and max_height to opts, so opts becomes an Integer and opts[:allow_animation] raises TypeError. The API contract for downsize is broken.

findings.title: In-place downsize overwrites source file
findings.body: In app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 67 the code calls OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) using the same path for source and destination. If convert/gifsicle fails, is killed, or partially writes, the original upload is truncated or corrupted with no backup. A failing conversion destroys the only copy before Upload.create_for runs. Use a separate temp file and replace only on success.

findings.title: Loop checks stale tempfile.size and ignores downsize failure
findings.body: In app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb the while condition uses tempfile.size after an external ImageMagick/ImageOptim process rewrites the file at tempfile.path, and line 72 passes the same tempfile.size to Upload.create_for. An open Tempfile descriptor does not reliably reflect an external truncate/replace, so the loop can run all 5 iterations even after the file is already under SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, over-shrinking to 0.8^5 of dimensions, and the filesize stored in the database can mismatch the bytes on disk. The return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is also ignored, so 5 failing converts are spawned on corrupt input and a corrupt file can still be passed to Upload.create_for.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10MB client limit ignores image vs attachment settings
findings.body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js validateUploadedFile replaced Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'] with hardcoded 10*1024. The server only downsizes images, not attachments, so attachments larger than max_attachment_size_kb but under 10MB now pass client validation only to fail server-side, and images are blocked at 10MB even if the admin raised max_image_size_kb above 10MB. The same hardcoding at line 246 for 413 errors shows users the wrong max_size_kb.

findings.title: Extension-only image check sends SVG and spoofed files to convert
findings.body: In app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb line 64 gating uses FileHelper.is_image?(filename), which checks the filename extension. Large SVG vectors will therefore be sent to convert -resize 80%, rasterizing/flattening a vector format that OptimizedImage.create_for explicitly avoids converting by copying. Conversely a large non-image renamed to .jpg triggers up to 5 ImageMagick processes, wasting CPU. Content/type validation and an SVG exclusion are needed.
